# 1 Enoch Chapter 28 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 1 Enoch Chapter 28 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 28:1 — "Erythraean Sea" identification

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the Erythraean sea" | Retains classical name without gloss |
| LOGOS | "the Erythraean Sea" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "the Erythraean Sea — the Red Sea" | Adds gloss for modern readers |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "the Erythraean Sea" without the gloss. "Erythraean Sea" is the ancient Greek/classical name for the body of water (roughly the modern Red Sea area), and it is sufficiently well known in this literary tradition to stand alone. PNEUMA's gloss is helpful but the text itself does not gloss it.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/EMET.

---

## 28:2 — description of the great bird

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a great bird [having on each of its wings an arm]" | Brackets for uncertain Ge'ez; unusual anatomical detail |
| LOGOS | "a great bird flying over the great sea" | Omits uncertain arm detail; focuses on action |
| PNEUMA | "an enormous bird soaring over the great sea" | "Enormous" for "great"; "soaring" for flying |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "a great bird flying over the great sea." EMET's bracketed "having on each of its wings an arm" reflects a difficult Ge'ez reading that is not well attested; LOGOS's simpler rendering is better. PNEUMA's "soaring" and "enormous" add interpretive color not present in the text.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 28:3 — "resembling clusters of vine grapes" vs. "like clusters of ripe grapes on a vine"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "resembling clusters of grapes of the vine" | Literal genitive construction |
| LOGOS | "resembling clusters of vine grapes" | Compressed genitive |
| PNEUMA | "like clusters of ripe grapes on a vine" | "Ripe" adds unwarranted detail |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "resembling clusters of vine grapes." EMET's "grapes of the vine" is natural in a Semitic idiom but slightly redundant in English. PNEUMA's "ripe" is an addition not in the Ge'ez.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
